title: Failed-Unit Disposal Charges — Bridgewell Homeowner Service Contracts Cash Offers
content:
On a company-elected offer worked out under the rule for replacements no network contractor can install, and only on such an offer, the cash carries the failed-unit disposal charge for work the homeowner's own installer must now do, and no supplemental allowance is booked; every other cash settlement and every out-of-network reimbursement remains under the general allowance rule. This applies to Homeowner Service Contracts.

The failed-unit disposal charge pays for taking away the failed unit the homeowner's installer removes:

- refrigerator or cooling system, whose refrigerant must be recovered: **80.00**;
- water heater or heating system: **45.00**;
- any other item: **nothing**.

It is added to the company-elected cash basis as a flat dollar amount, never compounded, and the basis so obtained is compared with the remaining item and aggregate benefits without being rounded first.

*Hypothetical:* a failed kitchen refrigerator, 80.00; a failed boiler (heating system), 45.00; a failed built-in microwave, nothing.
